responses: After thoughtful discussion with the committee, I’ve settled on a balanced yet forward-looking allocation that prioritizes both immediate operational gains and long-term workforce sustainability. I recommend 30% to AUTOMATION to drive efficiency and competitiveness in manufacturing, 25% to WORKFORCE_TRAINING to ensure our people can thrive in an AI-driven environment, 15% to EMPLOYEE_SUPPORT to address the human impact of transition and maintain morale, 20% to DATA_INFRASTRUCTURE to build the secure, scalable foundation needed for AI systems, and 10% to INNOVATION_LAB to foster future growth and differentiation. This mix reflects my belief that technology must serve people, and that investing in our employees is as critical as investing in machines. While some colleagues pushed for more innovation or automation, I’m convinced that without strong training and support, even the most advanced systems will fail to deliver their full potential.

I would recommend allocating 30% to WORKFORCE_TRAINING, 25% to DATA_INFRASTRUCTURE, 20% to AUTOMATION, 15% to EMPLOYEE_SUPPORT, and 10% to INNOVATION_LAB. The transition to AI must be people-centered—without reskilling and AI literacy, employees will feel left behind, undermining morale and productivity. Strong data infrastructure is foundational for any AI system to function securely and scalably, so investing here ensures long-term reliability. Automation will drive efficiency, but it should be implemented thoughtfully, not as a cost-cutting measure. Employee support is critical to manage anxiety and ensure a smooth transition. Finally, while innovation is exciting, it’s a longer-term play; we should prioritize stability and readiness before betting heavily on unproven R&D. This balance ensures we build capability, maintain trust, and lay the groundwork for sustainable growth.

I believe the $5 million AI transition budget should be allocated with a strong focus on people and long-term sustainability. I’d recommend about 30% to WORKFORCE_TRAINING, because reskilling our employees is essential for a smooth transition and ensures they can thrive in an AI-driven environment. Another 20% should go to EMPLOYEE_SUPPORT, recognizing that change can be stressful and we need to care for our team’s well-being during this shift. I’d allocate 25% to DATA_INFRASTRUCTURE, since robust data systems are the foundation for any AI initiative. The remaining 25% should be split between AUTOMATION (15%) and INNOVATION_LAB (10%), because while automation will boost efficiency, we also need to invest in future growth through innovation. This balance prioritizes our people while building the technical backbone and future potential of the company.
